title: Weak saturation in each variable of the pushout-join property
statement:
Use simplicial sets and horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A class of simplicial maps is weakly saturated if it contains all isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Inner anodyne maps are the weakly saturated class generated by $\Lambda_j^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ for $0<j<m$. The join $X\star Y$ has $r$-simplices $X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg\coprod_{u,v\geq0,\ u+v+1=r}X_u\times Y_v$, with simplicial operators restricting the ordered concatenation of the $X$-vertices followed by the $Y$-vertices. For monomorphisms $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $k:K\hookrightarrow L$, write
$$\theta_{i,k}:(A\star L)\amalg_{A\star K}(B\star K)\longrightarrow B\star L.$$
For each fixed monomorphism $k$, the class of monomorphisms $i$ for which $\theta_{i,k}$ is inner anodyne is weakly saturated. For each fixed monomorphism $i$, the class of monomorphisms $k$ for which $\theta_{i,k}$ is inner anodyne is weakly saturated.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation reductions, before the generating-horn calculation. Kerodon tag 018J (not the unrelated Stacks tag); read online, not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Use simplicial sets as functors to sets from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and the standard simplices of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A monomorphism is exactly a degreewise injection: an $r$-simplex $x$ gives the map $\Delta^r\to X$ sending $\alpha:[s]\to[r]$ to $X(\alpha)(x)$, so cancellation against these maps tests injectivity, and degreewise injectivity implies cancellation. Pushouts are degreewise set pushouts, and unions of increasing simplicial subsets are degreewise unions: the operators descend to the quotient or restrict to the union, and compatible degreewise maps give the universal map.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text: Identify the monomorphisms with their image inclusions. Write $D(i,k)=(A\star L)\cup(B\star K)\subseteq B\star L$. The intersection is $A\star K$, by the join formula in the statement, so this union is the displayed pushout. In degree $r$, $D(i,k)$ contains both pure summands $B_r,L_r$ and, in each mixed summand, exactly $(A_u\times L_v)\cup(B_u\times K_v)$ for $u+v+1=r$. Thus $\theta_{i,k}$ is its inclusion.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text: For maps $a:X\to X'$ and $b:Y\to Y'$, the join map acts as $a_r,b_r$ on pure summands and as $(x,y)\mapsto(a_u(x),b_v(y))$ on mixed summands. This commutes with ordered restriction, identities and composition, so commutative squares in $i,k$ induce commutative squares of $\theta$-maps. If either $i$ or $k$ is an isomorphism, the mixed-subset formula of Step 2 fills every mixed summand, hence $\theta_{i,k}$ is an isomorphism and is inner anodyne by definition. Finite composites are finite transfinite composites; composing with endpoint isomorphisms therefore preserves membership in the weakly saturated inner-anodyne class. This justifies replacing arbitrary monomorphisms by their image inclusions throughout.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text: The restriction to monomorphisms survives all three closure operations. Degreewise the pushout of $A\subseteq B$ along $A\to A'$ is $A'\amalg(B\setminus A)$, so its map from $A'$ is injective. Equality in an ordinal colimit is witnessed at a common later stage, since a finite zigzag has an upper bound; injectivity then shows that every stage embeds, and continuity identifies limit stages with unions. A retract of an injection is injective: apply the section on its source, cancel in the larger injection, and then apply the retraction on its source. These constructions commute with simplicial operators as in Step 1.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text: Fix $k:K\hookrightarrow L$. Push out $i_0:A_0\hookrightarrow B_0$ along an arbitrary map $A_0\to A'$ to obtain $i':A'\hookrightarrow B'=B_0\amalg_{A_0}A'$. The natural square with top row $D(i_0,k)\to B_0\star L$ and bottom row $D(i',k)\to B'\star L$ is a pushout: in degree $r$ the top row adds precisely $(B_{0,u}\setminus A_{0,u})\times(L_v\setminus K_v)$ in each mixed summand, and $B'_u=A'_u\amalg(B_{0,u}\setminus A_{0,u})$ shows that the bottom row adds exactly the same elements, without further identifications. Pure summands already belong to the domains. Hence $\theta_{i',k}$ is a pushout of $\theta_{i_0,k}$ and is inner anodyne whenever $\theta_{i_0,k}$ is.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text:
Let $(X_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\lambda}$ be a continuous ordinal chain of monomorphisms, represented by subsets of $X_\lambda$, and assume that every $\theta_{X_\alpha\hookrightarrow X_{\alpha+1},k}$ is inner anodyne. Inside $X_\lambda\star L$ put $P_\alpha=(X_\alpha\star L)\cup(X_\lambda\star K)$. For $\alpha<\lambda$, set $E_\alpha=(X_\alpha\star L)\cup(X_{\alpha+1}\star K)$. The mixed-subset formula gives
$$P_\alpha\cap(X_{\alpha+1}\star L)=E_\alpha,\qquad P_\alpha\cup(X_{\alpha+1}\star L)=P_{\alpha+1}.$$
Thus $P_\alpha\to P_{\alpha+1}$ is the pushout of $\theta_{X_\alpha\hookrightarrow X_{\alpha+1},k}:E_\alpha\to X_{\alpha+1}\star L$, so it is inner anodyne.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text: At every nonzero limit $\delta\leq\lambda$, the join formula gives $P_\delta=\bigcup_{\alpha<\delta}P_\alpha$: a mixed simplex involving $X_\delta$ has its $X$-coordinate in some earlier $X_\alpha$, while the fixed subset $X_\lambda\star K$ belongs to every stage. Thus the preceding chain is continuous, starts at $P_0=D(X_0\hookrightarrow X_\lambda,k)$ and ends at $P_\lambda=X_\lambda\star L$. Closure of inner anodyne maps under transfinite composition makes its composite $\theta_{X_0\hookrightarrow X_\lambda,k}$ inner anodyne. If $\lambda=0$ this is an isomorphism, already covered in Step 3.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text: If $i$ is a retract of $j$ in the category of maps, the section and retraction squares induce section and retraction squares between $\theta_{i,k}$ and $\theta_{j,k}$ by Step 3; their composite is the identity on both source and target because the original composite squares are identities. Thus $\theta_{i,k}$ is a retract of $\theta_{j,k}$, and retract closure of inner anodyne maps applies. Steps 3--7 and the preservation of monomorphisms in Step 4 establish every clause of weak saturation for fixed $k$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text: Now fix $i:A\hookrightarrow B$. Push out $k_0:K_0\hookrightarrow L_0$ along an arbitrary map $K_0\to K'$ to obtain $k':K'\hookrightarrow L'=L_0\amalg_{K_0}K'$. The square with top row $D(i,k_0)\to B\star L_0$ and bottom row $D(i,k')\to B\star L'$ is a pushout: its top row adds precisely $(B_u\setminus A_u)\times(L_{0,v}\setminus K_{0,v})$, and $L'_v=K'_v\amalg(L_{0,v}\setminus K_{0,v})$ identifies these with exactly the new elements of the bottom row; every pure simplex is already in its domain. Consequently $\theta_{i,k'}$ is a pushout of $\theta_{i,k_0}$, and inner-anodyne closure under pushout proves the required closure in $k$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text:
Let $(Y_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\lambda}$ be a continuous ordinal chain of monomorphisms with every $\theta_{i,Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y_{\alpha+1}}$ inner anodyne. Represent its stages as subsets of $Y_\lambda$ and put $Q_\alpha=(B\star Y_\alpha)\cup(A\star Y_\lambda)\subseteq B\star Y_\lambda$. For $\alpha<\lambda$, put $F_\alpha=(B\star Y_\alpha)\cup(A\star Y_{\alpha+1})$. Direct intersection and union of the mixed summands gives
$$Q_\alpha\cap(B\star Y_{\alpha+1})=F_\alpha,\qquad Q_\alpha\cup(B\star Y_{\alpha+1})=Q_{\alpha+1}.$$
Hence $Q_\alpha\to Q_{\alpha+1}$ is a pushout of $\theta_{i,Y_\alpha\hookrightarrow Y_{\alpha+1}}:F_\alpha\to B\star Y_{\alpha+1}$ and is inner anodyne.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text: For nonzero limit $\delta\leq\lambda$, a mixed simplex of $B\star Y_\delta$ has its $Y$-coordinate in some earlier $Y_\alpha$, and $A\star Y_\lambda$ is included at every stage; hence $Q_\delta=\bigcup_{\alpha<\delta}Q_\alpha$. Also $Q_0=D(i,Y_0\hookrightarrow Y_\lambda)$ and $Q_\lambda=B\star Y_\lambda$. The continuous composite of the inner anodyne successor maps in Step 10 is therefore $\theta_{i,Y_0\hookrightarrow Y_\lambda}$, and it is inner anodyne by transfinite-composition closure. For $\lambda=0$ use the isomorphism case of Step 3.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, proof: the two weak-saturation assertions; elementary degreewise details supplied here.

proof.text: Finally, if $k$ is a retract of $l$ as a map, applying the explicit join maps of Step 3 with the identity on $A,B$ and the given section and retraction on the second variable yields a retract of $\theta_{i,l}$ equal to $\theta_{i,k}$: composition is the identity on pure summands and on each coordinate of every mixed summand, and hence on the pushout domain. Retract closure makes $\theta_{i,k}$ inner anodyne when $\theta_{i,l}$ is. Together with the isomorphism case, Steps 9--11 and Step 4, this proves weak saturation for fixed $i$.
